steps: Position the stove
4" to side and back walls, 18" to the ceiling, 1" to the vent pipe. Any flooring that is stable and strong enough to carry the stove — no floor protector needed.

Interior side wall4"
Interior back wall4"
Interior ceiling18"
Venting pipe1"
  • Out of traffic and away from furniture and draperies.
  • Suitable for a bedroom or bed sitting room.
  • Aftermarket permanently located manufactured home (USA only) or mobile home, where local codes don't prohibit it; the stove must be fastened in place. Install per CAN/CSA Z240 MH (Canada) or Title 24 CFR, Part 3280 / ANSI/NFPA 501A (USA).
  • Installation and venting to CAN/CGA-B149 (Canada) or ANSI Z223.1 (USA) and local codes; qualified personnel only. Massachusetts: a licensed Plumber and Gas Fitter only.
Venting & termination

4" x 6 5/8" co-axial certified components only: 30 feet max total, max three 90° elbows, horizontal run reduced 2 feet for each 90° after the first. Snorkel terminal when the horizontal termination is no higher than 2 feet vertically.

Any rise/run combination inside the co-axial venting envelope (a diagram on p. 17); support the vent pipe properly. Certified 4" x 6 5/8" components are cross-referenced on p. 21 — don't mix manufacturers. Terminal clearances: see the vent terminal clearances card (p. 16).

Snorkel terminal (11270002)

  • Orient it with the vent inlet and outlet at the bottom end; otherwise exhaust is restricted.
  • Fasten to the exterior wall with the 4 supplied screws, drain ports at the bottom.
  • Siding can butt up to the sides and extend up to 1" from the wall.
  • Caulk where the unit meets the wall and where the siding meets the unit.

Co-linear through a chimney

  1. Measure the chimney; cut the flex liners (min. 10' to termination). Mark one pipe at both ends as the combustion air intake.
  2. Marked liner to the intake side of the vent terminal, the other to the outlet side; seal and secure with the sealant and screws provided.
  3. Insert both liners from the top of the chimney down through the damper opening.
  4. Run a bead of caulking on top of the clay liner, slip the terminal over the liner and secure it with the lateral retaining bolts.
  5. Larger chimneys: build flashing to local building codes.

Through an existing fireplace opening with a co-axial to co-linear adapter: seal the opening with a cover that lets the adapter sit flush, or position the stove and adapter outside the opening.

Note: p. 22 says the stove is certified for 4" x 6 5/8" coaxial venting components only, while p. 18 recommends co-linear 3" + 3" flex kits for this appliance.
Massachusetts (sidewall termination less than seven (7) feet above grade): hard-wired CO detector with alarm and battery back-up on the appliance's floor level, a CO detector with alarm on each additional level, and a metal or plastic sign at least eight (8) feet above grade in line with the terminal reading "GAS VENT DIRECTLY BELOW. KEEP CLEAR OF ALL OBSTRUCTIONS".
Gas & electrical connections

Position the stove, then connect the supply (connector not included) to the 3/8" 45° flare fitting at the rear, with a drip leg and a union just upstream of the valve. IEC power cord to a standard wall outlet; don't plug in or turn on the gas until installation is complete.

• Correct gas line diameter for proper operation and pressure; check local codes for additional requirements.
  • Drip leg in the supply line to the gas control valve, to keep loose scale or dirt out of the valve.
  • Union or flanged connection (not provided) just upstream of the valve, for valve repair or replacement.
  • Turn on the gas supply and check that all connections are tight and leak free.
  • Supply-piping pressure tests above ½ psig (3.5 kPa): disconnect the stove and its individual shut-off valve. At ½ psig (3.5 kPa) or less: close its manual shut-off valve.

Rear layout (Figure 33): left and right blower fans, battery holder, control module, gas supply connection, electrical plug-in, venturi adjustment, gas valve. Service from the rear by removing the access panel.

Line voltage: don't open or tamper with the control enclosure; disconnect line voltage before any maintenance. Label all wires before disconnecting them when servicing controls, and verify proper operation afterwards (wiring diagram, p. 38).
Open the firebox

Ceramic panels and burner ship installed; logs and embers are packed behind the glass door and screen. Lift off the top cover, raise the cover plate and lift out the screen, then remove the wing-nut bolts and lift out the glass door with its retainer frame.

1. Remove the top cover. The latticed oval panel in its center isn't fastened to it — don't let it slip off.
  2. Raise the glass door and safety screen cover and lift the safety screen out.
  3. Remove the wing nut bolts securing the glass door retainer frame to the stove frame; tilt the glass door and remove it together with its retainer frame.

The ceramic panels and gas burner come already installed. The log set and glowing embers are packed in protective styrofoam; the large rear log is wrapped separately from the smaller logs.

Maker's website: Interior: Preassembled interior with black porcelain panels and mature fire logset; floor illumination.
Log set & embers

Fill the burner tray with embers (reserve some), then set logs 1–5 in order: log 2 close to but not covering the pilot, logs 3 and 5 clear of the burner's back-row holes. Fill gaps with the reserved embers.

1. Fill the burner tray so the baskets are filled and overflowing the burners' front row; reserve a small amount of embers.
  2. Log 1 (large rear log) on the firebox ledge, completely set against the rear wall.
  3. Log 2: fit the hole in its back over the post on the left side of log 1; lower end close to the pilot without covering it, and as far forward as possible without interfering with the glass door.
  4. Log 3: the hole in its underside fits the protruding tab on the left side of the burner; it must not cover the back-row burner holes.
  5. Log 4: black charcoal side faces inwards; it supports the final log.
  6. Log 5: must not cover the back-row burner holes.
  7. Fill any left-over spaces with the reserved embers.

Final positions are shown in photos (Figures 46–51).

A few embers between the back burner and logs 3 and 4 will hide the back burner, but they impede airflow around it and a sooty flame may result.
Glass door & safety screen

Seat the glass door frame in the floor slot, align its positioning stud and tighten the bolts — over-tightening the wing bolts can fracture the glass. Screen rear side toward the logs, bottom edge in its channel, top in the holder; refit the top cover.

Glass door

  1. Lower the frame into place so it fits the horizontal slot on the firebox floor.
  2. Align it laterally so its protruding positioning stud fits the slot in the firebox; this lines up the bolt slots at the top of the frame.
  3. Insert and tighten the bolts.
Over-tightening the wing bolts could fracture the glass door.

Safety screen

  • Sits between the glass door and the doors, protecting against heat radiating from the glass.
  • Rear side faces the log set, front side faces the doors. The frame isn't square — orient it before inserting.
  • Bottom edge fits firmly into the channel in the firebox frame; lower the top holder so its channels secure the top of the mesh (a small amount of force may be needed).
  • Return the top cover without letting the loose oval panel slip off.
Initialize the controls

4 AA in the rear battery holder (selection switch on Remote), 3 AAA in the transmitter, plug in and open the gas. Press PRG with a straightened paper clip (module beeps 3 times), then the transmitter's power button (4 beeps = synchronized).

Proflame 2 IFC module: automatic ignition and pilot flame supervision, IPI or CPI, comfort fan off plus six speeds, a remotely actuated auxiliary outlet and a dimmable light outlet. AC powered, with the battery pack as backup only when line power is interrupted or lost.

  1. Install 4 AA batteries in the battery holder on the rear of the stove; selection switch on the switch cover set to "Remote".
  2. Install 3 AAA batteries in the Proflame 2 remote transmitter.
  3. Plug the power cord into a wall socket and open the gas supply line.
  4. Insert a straightened paper clip into the "PRG" opening of the ON/OFF battery holder and press the program button once; the module beeps 3 times, ready to synchronize.
  5. Push the transmitter's power on button once; it beeps 4 times when transmitter and module are synchronized.

Pilot mode: with the system off, Mode to the CPI icon; Up = CPI, Down = IPI. The pilot may take up to 30 seconds to ignite each time ON is selected.
Damper & venturi
Damper (under the top cladding cover plate) ships closed: open slowly as needed to eliminate a sagging, sooting flame. Venturi (opening in the rear cover): closed for natural gas, open for propane.

Damper

Under the top cladding cover plate (+ = open, − = closed). Factory setting is closed; slowly open and adjust as necessary to eliminate a sagging, sooting flame. Every venting configuration is different, so slight adjustment may be needed.

Venturi

Through an opening in the rear cover (Figure 33). Loosen the wing nut, move the post up to open or down to close, then tighten the wing nut. Closed for natural gas, open for liquid propane.
Gas pressure check

Gas off before loosening the valve test-point screws (behind the back panel); fit the gauge, then verify pressure with the stove lit at its highest setting. Gas off, gauges off, re-tighten the screws.

Inlet · NG min / max5.0" WC / 13.9" WC
Inlet · LP min / max12.5" WC / 13.9" WC
Manifold · NG high / low3.8" WC / 1.1" WC
Manifold · LP high / low11" WC / 2.9" WC
  1. Remove the back panel and locate the valve.
  2. Locate the inlet and outlet test points on the valve (Figure 72 labels them inlet pressure and manifold pressure); loosen the screws in the ports with a flat-tip screwdriver.
  3. Attach the pressure gauge to the test ports.
  4. Turn the gas supply back on and verify pressure with the stove lit on its highest setting.
  5. Turn off the gas supply, remove the gauges and re-tighten the test-point screws.

Pilot flame: adjust with the pilot flame level adjustment screw on the valve, using a flat-tip screwdriver.
Propane conversion (if LP)

Gas off, stove cooled to room temperature. Kit 12180005 supplies new pilot and burner orifices and a pressure modulator; remove the mesh and glass doors, logs, embers and burner to reach the orifices, then open the venturi.

1. Shut off the gas supply and let the stove cool to room temperature.
  2. Pressure modulator: follow the instructions provided with the conversion kit.
  3. Remove the mesh and glass doors, log set, embers and burner.
  4. Burner orifice (lower inside rear of the firebox): remove with a ½" socket; apply Loctite 567 Thread Sealant to the threads of the new orifice before installing.
  5. Pilot orifice: remove the spring, then pull the pilot hood up off the pilot bracket. Turn the orifice out counter-clockwise with a 5/32" or 4mm Allen wrench; tighten the new one to 9 lbf in (1 Nm). Refit the hood (tab on its base to the slot in the pilot journal) and push the spring onto its seat.
  6. Adjust the venturi shutter to the open (propane) setting.

Burner orifices are marked "EA" for natural gas and "EB" for propane.

panels.title: Sagging or sooty flame
items: Damper too closed (factory setting is closed) → open slowly until the sagging, sooting flame clears
Embers placed between the back burner and logs 3–4 → airflow around the back burner impeded, sooty flame may result
Excessive soot on logs, embers or burners at the annual check → qualified service person to inspect and adjust for proper combustion

panels.title: Burner won't light or stay lit
items: Pilot slow after ON → normal; it may take up to 30 seconds to ignite
First lighting → allow time for air to escape from the gas lines
No light → turn off, wait at least 5 minutes for gas to escape, retry; stop if you smell gas
Won't light or stay lit after several tries → off, all electric power off, call a service technician or gas supplier

panels.title: Remote or receiver signals
items: Low-battery icon on the remote screen → transmitter's 3 AAA batteries low
Module double-beeps when it receives a command → IFC backup batteries (4 AA) low
Receiver or transmitter batteries depleted → turn the stove off with the ON/OFF switch on the rear battery holder (manual bypass)

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
Your stove lights itself: an ignition device lights the pilot automatically. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

  1. Smell for gas first. Sniff all around the stove, including next to the floor, because some gas is heavier than air and settles low. If you smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety.
  2. Turn it on. With the system off, press the ON/OFF key on the remote. The stove beeps once. The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light.
  3. If the burner lights, set the flame and other settings with the remote.
  4. If it doesn't light, turn it off. Wait at least 5 minutes for any gas inside to clear. If you still smell gas, stop and follow the gas-smell steps under Safety and a gas smell. If you don't, try again.
  5. If it won't light or stay lit after several tries, turn it off, turn off all electric power to the stove and call your service technician or gas supplier.
Lighting it for the first time? Allow extra time for air to escape from the gas lines.
Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the stove and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs on 3 AAA batteries. It has an ON/OFF key, a Thermostat key, Up/Down arrows and a Mode key. The stove beeps once each time it receives a command.

On and off

Press ON/OFF to turn the stove on. Press it again to turn it off. The screen then shows only the room temperature.

Flame height

There are six flame levels. Press Down to lower the flame one step at a time, all the way to off. Press Up to raise it. If you press Up while the system is on but the flame is off, the flame comes on at high.

Key lock

To stop unsupervised use, press Mode and Up together. A lock icon appears. Press them together again to unlock.

°F or °C

With the remote off, press Thermostat and Mode together. Check that a C or F shows to the right of the room temperature.

Mode also steps to the fan, accent light and pilot settings.

It can start suddenly. The control lights the stove, and it can turn on without warning. Keep away from the burner when you use the remote.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
For everyday use, press ON/OFF on the remote while the stove is on. The stove beeps once, and the remote's screen goes back to showing only the room temperature.

Batteries low or dead?

If the batteries in the remote or in the stove's control are low or dead, you can turn the stove off by hand. Use the ON/OFF switch on the battery holder at the back of the stove. This bypasses the remote.

For service or a long shutdown

  1. Turn the stove off.
  2. Turn off all electric power to the stove.
  3. Take out the backup batteries.

Before any servicing, also turn off the gas and give the stove plenty of time to cool.

sounds.title: First fire: smells, sounds and beeps
sounds.html:
A smell for the first couple of hours

The first time it's lit, the stove gives off a slight odor for a couple of hours. That's the paints, sealants, gaskets and lubricants curing. It's temporary. Open doors and windows to air the room, because the smell can bother some people.

Ticking and creaking

Steel stoves make some expansion and contraction noises as they warm up and cool down. Your furnace and oven make similar noises. It's normal.

Beeps from the stove

  • One beep: the stove received your remote command.
  • A double beep when it receives a command: the backup batteries in the stove's control are low.

A short wait to light

The pilot can take up to 30 seconds to light each time you turn the stove on. The very first lighting can take longer, while air escapes from the gas lines.

thermostat.title: Thermostat and Smart mode
thermostat.html:
The remote can work as a room thermostat, so the stove holds the comfort level you choose. The Thermostat key turns it on or off and steps through its functions.

Room thermostat

  1. Press Thermostat. The screen shows the thermostat is on, with the set temperature.
  2. Press Up or Down until the temperature you want shows.

Smart thermostat

Smart mode changes the flame height to match how far the room is from your set temperature. As the room gets close, it turns the flame down. If the room is cool, it turns the flame up.

  1. Press Thermostat until the word SMART appears to the right of the temperature icon.
  2. Press Up or Down to set the temperature you want.

settings.title: Fan, accent light and pilot mode
settings.html:
Press Mode on the remote to step to each of these settings, then use the arrows. The stove beeps once to confirm.

Comfort fan

The hot-air circulating fan has six speeds. Step to the fan icon, then use Up/Down to turn the fan on, off, or change its speed.

Accent light

The light bulb icon controls the accent lighting, in six brightness levels. Use Up/Down to set it.

The stove comes with glass plates in several colours, in a tray underneath the stove. To change one, slide a new plate into the holder under the light tray, from the front of the stove. Let the plate cool first.

Pilot mode

You can choose continuous pilot (CPI) or intermittent pilot (IPI). With the system off, press Mode until you reach the CPI icon. Press Up for continuous pilot, or Down to go back to intermittent.

power.title: Batteries and power
power.html:
The stove plugs into a standard wall outlet. A battery pack backs up the control, and those batteries are used only when house power is interrupted or lost.

Backup · battery holder at the back4 AA
Remote3 AAA

Low-battery signs

  • Remote: a battery icon appears on the screen before the power runs out. It goes away once you fit new batteries.
  • Backup batteries: the stove double-beeps when it receives a command. With new batteries it goes back to a single beep.

If the batteries are low or dead, you can still turn the stove off with the ON/OFF switch on the battery holder. Check and replace batteries as needed at each yearly inspection.

Pairing the remote

The switch on the battery holder stays on Remote. To pair, push a straightened paper clip into the opening marked PRG on the battery holder and press once (the stove beeps 3 times). Then press the remote's power button once (it beeps 4 times when paired).

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the viewing glass whenever it needs it, with fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Only clean the glass when it's cool, never while it's hot.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners on the glass, or on any other part of the stove.
  • Don't strike or knock the glass. It can break.

Cracked or broken glass

Don't run the stove with the glass door cracked, broken or removed. Replace it before you use the stove again. Get a replacement glass door from your Pacific Energy dealer, don't substitute any other type, and have a licensed or qualified service person fit it.

The rest of the stove

Clean the outside finish with mild soap and water.

Hot glass causes burns. Don't touch the glass until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.

service.title: Yearly inspection
service.html:
Have a qualified service person inspect the stove and its venting before use and at least once a year. You may need it cleaned more often if there's a lot of lint from carpets or bedding. The control compartment, burners and air passages must stay clean.

What the yearly check covers

  1. Glass door, logs and embers removed, and checked with the burners for soot. Heavy soot means the stove needs adjusting for proper combustion. Burners cleaned with a brush or vacuum, paying close attention to the burner ports.
  2. Pilot checked for proper flame size and operation, and cleaned.
  3. Vent pipe and outside vent terminal checked for blockage or debris.
  4. Glass gasket checked and replaced if needed. The glass seal must stay in good condition.
  5. Batteries checked and replaced as needed.
Turn off the gas and electric power and let the stove cool well before any servicing. If you find a problem, call your dealer. Don't try to repair the stove yourself.

Keep the area around the stove clear of anything that burns, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

safety.title: Safety and a gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbour's phone and follow their instructions.
  • If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.

Hot surfaces

  • The stove and its glass get very hot. Keep children, clothing and furniture away, and watch young children closely when they're in the room.
  • A barrier that reduces burns from the hot glass comes with the stove and must be installed. For toddlers and other at-risk people, an adjustable safety gate can keep them out of the room.
  • Keep gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids away from the stove.
  • Put back any panel or door removed for service before you use the stove.
Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect the stove and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

review.notes: Models: the manual covers MODEL: TRENTON, SERIES: A (p. 1) and never uses the name Trenton Classic. It separates finishes only by sales code (Metalic Black 12020003, Antique White 12020001, Majolica Brown 12020002) and by replacement cast iron kit (Painted 80002066 incl. top grill; Antique White 80002063 and Maj Brown 80002064 incl. front and doors), all on p. 37. Every rating, pressure, dimension, clearance and vent limit is printed once, so the only per-model rows are those per-finish codes (spec card 'parts'). Rows are labelled by finish because the Classic = Antique White / Majolica Brown mapping comes from the catalog features, not the manual; the manual's 'Metalic' is spelled 'Metallic' on the page. The p. 18 co-linear notes call the appliance 'TN24' (not defined elsewhere; the figure is captioned 'Trenton co-linear venting configuration'). The rating label (p. 39) is an image with no text and no listing standard appears anywhere, so 'certification' is omitted. Not in the manual text: minimum input rate, weight, electrical rating, viewing/glass area, blower cfm, levelling legs, heat-exchanger fins, warranty terms (only 'voids the warranty', p. 4), a troubleshooting chart or code table. Fault panels use the manual's own fault statements (pp. 6, 8, 11, 12, 13, 28, 33); codes left empty. Catalog feature 'black porcelain panels': the manual says ceramic panels (p. 24) and 'Panel Set Painted' (p. 37). Shown only as diagrams, not transcribed: venting envelope (p. 17), adjacent-structure clearances (Figure 23, p. 16), location examples (Figures 21-22, p. 15), Snorkel dimensions (p. 19), log placement photos (pp. 26-28), wiring diagram (p. 38). The lighting label (p. 13) says 'push the On/Off switch'; the owner drawer uses the remote ON/OFF key described on p. 8. Label item C (gas control knob: use only your hand, never tools, don't repair it, force or attempted repair may cause fire or explosion) is shown as a danger note in the lighting drawer, although the lighting procedure itself uses no knob. p. 1 has offset-font text decoded with the 29-code-point rule: 'buildingK pbof^i @' = 'building. SERIAL #'. Pages 2-3 carry footer revision 040919-40; all others 130323-40.
